learningObjective: Identify factors that can invalidate torch.compile's compilation cache and cause re-compilation.
stem: Which of the following changes are expected to cause a torch.compile cache miss (and thus a fresh compile) rather than being served from the compilation cache? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Restarting the Python process without any persistent-cache mechanism enabled.
Passing a tensor on a different device (e.g., moving from `cuda:0` to `cuda:1`, or from CUDA to CPU).
Changing the input tensor's dtype (e.g., from FP32 to FP16) between calls.
Passing a tensor with the same shape, dtype, device, and stride as the previous call.

explanation: A: dtype guards fail on dtype change, forcing recompile. B: without a persistent cache (like the FX-graph cache / Inductor cache extensions in some configs), a process restart loses the in-memory compile cache. D: device changes fail device guards. C is a cache hit: matching shape/dtype/device/stride reuses the compiled variant.

optionExplanations.D: Wrong: this is exactly the cache-hit case.

assumptions: No persistent Inductor cache is enabled to survive across process restarts.
nonImplications: Does not imply the in-memory compile cache can never be persisted; recent releases include experimental persistent-cache mechanisms.
Does not imply that the cache key is exclusively (shape, dtype, device, stride); source-code hashes and other guards also participate.

distractorRationales.D: Wrong claim; matching metadata is a hit.
